headline: North-West SLA failures triggered enterprise churn, driving most of the revenue drop.
body: Fulfilment SLA in North-West degraded sharply, and WH-07 backlog is the operational root cause [E4]. Two enterprise accounts paused or threatened to pause orders after repeated late deliveries, directly cutting revenue [E1]. Enterprise account count fell in parallel, consistent with the SLA-driven churn story [E5]. Complaint rate rose too, but its comovement is weaker and looks more like a downstream symptom than an independent cause [E3].

actions.action: Add 3PL overflow capacity to clear WH-07 backlog
actions.expected_impact: Restore SLA and stop further account attrition
actions.monitoring: Daily SLA % and WH-07 backlog age

actions.action: Offer SLA guarantee to Meridian and Kalinga accounts
Adjust delivery promise messaging until SLA recovers
actions.expected_impact: Reduce complaint volume from mismatched expectations

what_could_change: Confirmation that WH-07 backlog is clearing and enterprise accounts resume orders would validate the fix; renewed SLA misses would overturn it.
caveats: Marketing conversion drop is flagged but has no supporting evidence snippets, so its role is unverified.
